why_this_exists: Round 42 gave the FILL axis a null and found the two axes disagree: CONDVALUE beats matched-random per fill and is worse than a blind cancel per cancel (2.865 vs 2.227 c/cancel). But the 2.227 figure is a POINT with no dispersion -- it is DE's analytic construction, `fills_per_generation` (1.1175861) x `book_mean_pnl_per_fill` (1.9927599). '1.29x worse than a blind cancel' therefore cannot be told from noise, which is the same defect the -953.92c delta carried before it got a null. The cancel axis now gets the same treatment the fill axis got.
THE_QUESTION_THIS_EXISTS_TO_ANSWER: IS THE CASCADE A PROPERTY OF CONDVALUE'S SELECTION, OR OF THE POLICY MACHINERY? CONDVALUE loses 4.32 fills per cancel and HAZARD 2.23, against DE's ASSUMED blind-cancel rate of 1.1176 fills per generation. If random cancel DECISIONS replayed through the same stateful policy also cascade at ~4x, the cascade is machinery and not selection, and the round-42 lever finding changes again. That is the decisive cell and it is named before the draw.

REPRODUCTION_GATE_ALREADY_PASSED_BEFORE_.baseline: all-zero scores through HSP.replay_policy give cancels_issued 0 and 4315 fills -- the same book the 701% ceiling was computed over
REPRODUCTION_GATE_ALREADY_PASSED_BEFORE_.meaning: BOTH ARMS REPRODUCE EXACTLY through the harness this null runs on. The null and the arms are on identical machinery, checked rather than argued.

THE_MATCHED_UNIT_IS_THE_DECISION_COUNT_A.ruling: R-521 -- the decision is the unit; rows are actions (CLAUDE.md rule 2)
THE_MATCHED_UNIT_IS_THE_DECISION_COUNT_A.measured_divergence: a decision count does NOT equal a realised cancel count. CONDVALUE makes 1,154 DECISIONS and issues 333 cancels (28.9%); HAZARD makes 106 and issues 48 (45.3%). A probe flagging 333 generations issued only 160 cancels. Matching the realised count would require solving for a decision count, which is the exact-set matching the V2 samplers could not do.
THE_MATCHED_UNIT_IS_THE_DECISION_COUNT_A.what_is_NOT_matched: the realised cancel count, the realised cancel SET, and the fills lost. All three are OUTCOMES here and are reported as distributions.
THE_MATCHED_UNIT_IS_THE_DECISION_COUNT_A.denominator_of_the_reported_statistic: cents_per_cancel divides by each draw's OWN realised cancels_issued, exactly as the arms' 2.8646 = 953.918/333 does. The ratio therefore remains comparable even though the counts differ.

STRATA.side: matched to each arm's OWN per-side decision counts -- CONDVALUE {BUY_UP 586, SELL_UP 568}, HAZARD {BUY_UP 41, SELL_UP 65}
STRATA.hour: DEGENERATE -- there is exactly one hour, so matching on hour is vacuous. Said here so the 'count/side/hour' construction is not read as having done work it did not do.
STRATA.note: this null CAN do the side matching the round-42 fill null could not: the arm's own event stream carries side, whereas the filed artifact carried fills_lost only as a total.

N_AND_ITS_HEADROOM_DECLARED_FROM_A_MEASU.projected_wall_s: 500 x 2 x ~0.35 = ~350 s plus overhead; inside the ten-minute bar
N_AND_ITS_HEADROOM_DECLARED_FROM_A_MEASU.why_not_larger: n = 1000 per cell projects to ~12 minutes, over the bar. n = 500 is the largest round number that fits, and it is declared BEFORE the draw rather than shrunk after seeing.
N_AND_ITS_HEADROOM_DECLARED_FROM_A_MEASU.memory_ceiling: 8G, this seat's cap, NOT raised (R-174). Measured peak 0.29 GB leaves the cap far from binding; the binding constraint is WALL TIME.
N_AND_ITS_HEADROOM_DECLARED_FROM_A_MEASU.family_composition: 2 arms x 3 statistics (cents_per_cancel, fills_lost_per_cancel, fills_lost). Every cell reported; none selected.
N_AND_ITS_HEADROOM_DECLARED_FROM_A_MEASU.headroom: floor 1/501 = 0.001996 against 0.05/6 = 0.008333 gives 4.17x headroom. n = 200 gives a floor of 0.004975 and only 1.68x.
N_AND_ITS_HEADROOM_DECLARED_FROM_A_MEASU.the_binding_constraint_is_not_n: as in round 42: the floor is not what limits this. CONSUMED DATA is.

THE_STATISTICS.primary: cents_per_cancel = (spread_forgone - adverse_saved) / cancels_issued, i.e. the cost of a cancel. LOWER IS BETTER, so the rank is one-sided in the LOW direction.
THE_STATISTICS.secondary: fills_lost_per_cancel -- the cascade. Reported with NO directional alternative because the question is whether the arm's 4.32 is UNUSUAL, not whether it is good.
THE_STATISTICS.rank_location: p = (1 + #{draws at least as extreme as observed}) / (n + 1), direction stated per statistic
THE_STATISTICS.reported_as: a LOCATION in a dispersion, NEVER a validation p-value

INSTRUMENTS_OF_RECORD_DELEGATED_NOT_COPI.replay: harmful_stateful_policy.replay_policy -- the cascade is REALISED by the machinery, never assumed
INSTRUMENTS_OF_RECORD_DELEGATED_NOT_COPI.separation: de_phase4_diag_runner.cancel_mechanics -- its cascade/selectivity decomposition and its `separation` block are CALLED, not reimplemented
INSTRUMENTS_OF_RECORD_DELEGATED_NOT_COPI.this_seat_adds: the random decision draw and the ranking. Q-BE-271 is the round this seat caught itself keeping a second copy of a DE instrument; it does not keep one here.

NO_HEAD_IS_VERIFIED_FOR_A_RANDOM_STREAM_: de_score_stream.score_events REQUIRES a verified head manifest, correctly -- an adapter that could score without one could score an unbound file. A random policy HAS no head, so this module builds the event list directly in the shape HSP.validate_scores demands and passes it to HSP.validate_scores explicitly. Borrowing a real head's manifest to get through the adapter would be a FALSE PROVENANCE CLAIM, and is refused.

WHAT_WOULD_COUNT.the_cascade_is_MACHINERY_not_selection: the null's fills_lost_per_cancel distribution contains 4.32. Then CONDVALUE's cascade is unremarkable and the round-42 cancel-axis reading needs correcting.
WHAT_WOULD_COUNT.the_cascade_is_SELECTION: 4.32 sits outside the null's distribution. Then CONDVALUE cancels generations with unusually many downstream fills, and that is a property of what it picks.
WHAT_WOULD_COUNT.DEs_analytic_blind_rate_is_WRONG: the null centres materially away from 1.1176, in which case the 2.227 c/cancel figure that round 42 compared against is itself mis-specified and BOTH arms' cancel-axis readings move
WHAT_WOULD_COUNT.the_arm_is_worse_than_random_cancelling: CONDVALUE's 2.8646 sits in the BAD tail of the null's cents_per_cancel
WHAT_WOULD_COUNT.NOT_DECLARED: any criterion that would close or open the cancellation lever. One consumed hour cannot support one.
